services.name: M38A1 Jeep
services.desc: At the DeLand Naval Air Station Museum, we honor not only the aircraft that shaped military history but also the ground vehicles that kept operations moving. One such icon is the M38A1 Jeep, a rugged and reliable military utility vehicle that served from the 1950s through the Vietnam War. The M38A1, produced from 1952 to 1971, was an evolution of the famous WWII Willys Jeep. Featuring a rounded hood, improved suspension, and a powerful Hurricane F-Head 4-cylinder engine, this jeep was built to handle rough terrain, extreme weather, and heavy military use. services.name: Sikorsky HO5S-1 (S-52) Helicopter
services.desc: At the DeLand Naval Air Station Museum, history comes to life through incredible aircraft like the Sikorsky HO5S-1 (S-52) helicopter, a Korean War-era MASH evacuation helicopter that played a vital role in saving lives on the battlefield. MASH Stands for Mobile Army Surgical Hospital. The HO5S-1, built by Sikorsky in 1952, was a lifeline for wounded troops during the Korean War. Operating as a MASH (Mobile Army Surgical Hospital) evacuation transport, this helicopter rushed injured soldiers from the front lines to field hospitals for stabilization before transferring them to hospital ships in Inchon Harbor.
